```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this
# document, and into whatever else needs it, which reads the errata_entries.csv written at
# the bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here, \was{} in an edition. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be
# set by either.
#
# Numbering is APPEND-ONLY once this note is published: an entry can already have been
# cited, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved.
#
# claim_ids names the ground-truth rows an entry corrects, semicolon-separated. Every entry
# is empty: every table_a4 cell reproduces, so no value row changes; entry 1 corrects a
# heading, entry 2 a sentence that lists tables, entries 3 to 6 the article's mathematics and
# entry 7 a panel title the regenerated figure already spells correctly.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids,

  1, "label", "pipeline", "full",
  "Supplementary Table A4 is headed as Placebo Test I and reports Placebo Test II",
  "published supplement p. 6, Table A4",
  "Table A4: Study A (Direct First): Placebo Test [[I]]",
  "Table A4: Study A (Direct First): Placebo Test [[II]]",
  paste("Table A3, directly above it on the same page, is Placebo Test I: its estimates sit",
        "near one and its n is the count of admitters for each item (327, 281, 31, 42,",
        "206). Table A4's estimates sit near zero and its n is 506, the full Study A sample,",
        "in every row, which is the form of Placebo Test II and the form of Table A7, its",
        "Study B counterpart, headed correctly on the next page. Every cell of Table A4",
        "reproduces from the deposited data as Placebo Test II. Only the heading is wrong."),
  "",

  2, "cross_reference", "reading", "full",
  "The supplement's list of placebo tables omits Table A4",
  "published supplement p. 5",
  "Of particular note are the results of the placebo tests, presented in Tables [[A3, A6, and A7]].",
  "Of particular note are the results of the placebo tests, presented in Tables [[A3, A4, A6, and A7]].",
  paste("The supplement reports four placebo tables, two for each study: Tables A3 and A4 for",
        "Study A and Tables A6 and A7 for Study B, each pair a Placebo Test I and a Placebo",
        "Test II. The sentence lists three. It leaves out Table A4, the Study A Placebo Test",
        "II, while naming its Study B counterpart, Table A7. The omission is of a piece with",
        "entry 1: with Table A4 headed as a second Placebo Test I, the headings distinguish",
        "three placebo tables rather than four, and the sentence names the three. The sentences",
        "that follow it, which count the questions failing each study's placebo test, are",
        "unchanged."),
  "",

  3, "definition", "remaster", "full",
  "Display (2) writes the noise term for its expectation",
  "published p. 48, display (2)",
  "$\\mathrm{E}[V_i \\mid Z_i = 1] - \\mathrm{E}[V_i \\mid Z_i = 0] = {}$[[$W_i + \\mu - W_i$]]${} = \\mu.$",
  "$\\mathrm{E}[V_i \\mid Z_i = 1] - \\mathrm{E}[V_i \\mid Z_i = 0] = {}$[[$\\mathrm{E}[W_i] + \\mu - \\mathrm{E}[W_i]$]]${} = \\mu.$",
  paste("Both sides of the display are expectations. Under Assumptions 2 and 3 the two",
        "conditional expectations are $\\mathrm{E}[W_i] + \\mu$ and $\\mathrm{E}[W_i]$, so the",
        "middle term equates a constant to the random variable $W_i$ where it means its",
        "expectation. The term cancels either way, and the display's conclusion, that the",
        "difference in expectations is $\\mu$, is unaffected."),
  "",

  4, "label", "remaster", "full",
  "Two sentences on the direct-question admitters print the estimand where they mean its estimate",
  "published p. 56",
  "difference-in-means estimate [[$\\beta$]] should be equal\n\nNone of the values of [[$\\beta$]] are",
  "difference-in-means estimate [[$\\hat{\\beta}$]] should be equal\n\nNone of the values of [[$\\hat{\\beta}$]] are",
  paste("The article defines $\\beta$ as a difference in conditional expectations, a",
        "population quantity, and its estimate as the difference in means $\\hat{\\beta}$, whose",
        "test against 1 is the one the article proposes. Both sentences are about the estimates",
        "computed from the data and the tests of them: an estimate is what should equal 1",
        "under Assumptions 1 to 4, and values are what can be significantly different from it.",
        "The quantity in each is $\\hat{\\beta}$. The reported results are unchanged."),
  "",

  5, "definition", "remaster", "full",
  "The proof of Lemma 2 orders on direct responses of one where it means zero",
  "published p. 62",
  "where we have reordered the indices so that [[$Y_1 = \\cdots = Y_k = 1$]].",
  "where we have reordered the indices so that [[$Y_1 = \\cdots = Y_k = 0$]].",
  paste("The proof conditions on exactly $k$ direct responses being zero, which is what",
        "$1 - \\bar{Y} = k/n$ says, and display (4), which the sentence describes, conditions on",
        "$Y_j = 0$ for $j = 1, \\ldots, k$. The reordering puts those $k$ units first, so their",
        "direct responses are zero, not one. The display is right and the sentence that",
        "glosses it is not; the proof is unaffected."),
  "",

  6, "typography", "remaster", "full",
  "Display (7) drops the comma before the last index of a range",
  "published p. 63, display (7)",
  "[[$Y_j = 0$ for $j = 1, \\ldots k$]]",
  "[[$Y_j = 0$ for $j = 1, \\ldots, k$]]",
  paste("The second line of display (7) prints the index range without the comma before $k$",
        "that every other range in the proof of Lemma 2 carries, including the next line",
        "of the same display."),
  "",

  7, "spelling", "remaster", "full",
  "A panel title in Figure A1 misspells Variability",
  "published supplement p. 3, Figure A1",
  "[[Varibility]] of responses to non-sensitive items",
  "[[Variability]] of responses to non-sensitive items",
  paste("The title of Figure A1's fourth panel. The figure as regenerated from the maintained",
        "code prints the word correctly."),
  ""
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

spell <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
  stopifnot(n >= 1, n <= length(words))
  words[n]
}

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
# An entry quoting two passages separates them with a blank line, which ends a blockquote.
quote <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\n\n", "\n>\n> ")

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one.
emit <- function(ns) walk(ns, function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ",
      str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ", quote(bold(e$published)),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", quote(bold(e$corrected)), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

This note lists `r spell(nrow(entries))` corrections to "Combining List Experiment and Direct Question Estimates of Sensitive Behavior Prevalence," published in *Journal of Survey Statistics and Methodology* 3(1):43--66, doi [10.1093/jssam/smu023](https://doi.org/10.1093/jssam/smu023). **None changes a number or a conclusion of the paper.** Four are in the article's mathematics: an expectation missing from display (2), the estimand printed for its estimate in two sentences, a condition in the proof of Lemma 2 stated as one where the proof requires zero, and a missing comma. Three are in the online supplement: the heading of a table, the sentence that lists the placebo tables, and a misspelled panel title.

Entry 1 was found by the maintained replication, which recomputes every cell of the supplement's tables from the deposited data and checks each against the printed value. Entry 2 was found on reading the supplement while the first was filed, and follows from it. Entries 3 to 7 were found while the article and supplement were reset for the remastered edition, which reads every page beside the published one. The code supporting the maintained analysis is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/aronow_etal_2015](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/aronow_etal_2015).

# The article

```{r article-entries, results="asis"}
emit(filter(entries, !str_detect(location, "supplement"))$entry)
```

# The online supplement

```{r supplement-entries, results="asis"}
emit(filter(entries, str_detect(location, "supplement"))$entry)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
